mechanism: Garlic has mild antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties that may theoretically increase bleeding risk, while morphine can cause constipation and gastrointestinal effects; garlic may have minimal CYP3A4 inhibition affecting morphine metabolism.
action: No dose adjustment typically required; monitor for unusual bleeding or bruising if garlic supplementation is used in high doses, particularly in patients on concurrent anticoagulants.
